findings.reason: the stated complement is narrower than the guarantee the node.py comment requires, so the node could key the fix on worktree/pid and silently reopen the pre-spawn race with no case reddening.
findings.text: §18's deliverable keeps refusing only for "a run that has a worktree or a worker process", but a run in the pre-spawn phase `starting` has neither a worktree nor a pid and its claim must still bind: `claim_disposition` returns "run ... records no worker process yet" (reckon/crew/node.py:1480-1489) precisely to close the window between pointer write and worker spawn, and `_UNLAUNCHED_CLAIM_PHASES` names that phase (reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:121-123, written at :606). A node implementing the criterion literally would make a starting run's claim non-binding and let a queued request launch over its paths — the collision the cited comment says the guard exists to prevent — and none of the five done-when cases exercises a queued request overlapping a `starting` run.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every path §18 cites resolves: `reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py` (`_repository_scope_claims` at :222), `reckon/crew/node.py` (`claim_disposition` at :1450), `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py` and `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` all exist; only the new test file it names is still to be created, as expected.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each of §18's five cases is measurable and the section names a declared negative control ("count queued pointers as claims again; the first two cases must then fail with the requests refusing each other").
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §18 logs its control "under the run directory", a durable crew-store path, not a scratchpad or a node-local temporary.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §18 introduces no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags; the test file it names (`test_overlapping_queued_requests_launch_in_turn.py`) reads by mechanism.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §18's root cause (a queued pointer has no pid, so `claim_disposition` keeps it binding) matches the cited code, but the deliverable's keep-refusing criterion ("a run that has a worktree or a worker process") omits the pre-spawn window the same code keeps binding, and no case guards it.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §18 carries one deliverable (a queued pointer's path claim stops binding) with five cases over it.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §18 declares no depends-on/gates link, and the sections it could contend with (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py` with §11/§14/§15, `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` with §12/§13/§14) are refused a second concurrent claim by dispatch's scope check, the same treatment the plan accepted for its other shared-file pairs.
